title: Martha's Rule Expands to All Emergency Departments in England
subtitle: A new system allows patients and families to request urgent medical reviews to improve safety.

summary.en: The NHS is expanding 'Martha's Rule' to every emergency department in England. This initiative allows patients, families, and staff to request an urgent second opinion if they feel a patient's condition is getting worse. The rule is named after 13-year-old Martha Mills, who died in 2021 after her health concerns were not properly addressed. Since its introduction in 2024, the system has already led to thousands of calls and potentially saved hundreds of lives. The full rollout across all emergency units is expected to be finished by March 2028.
summary.zh: 英國國民保健署正將「瑪莎條款」擴展至英格蘭所有急診部門。這項計畫允許病患、家屬及工作人員在認為病患狀況惡化時，要求緊急的第二醫療意見。該條款以二〇二一年因健康疑慮未獲妥善處理而過世的十三歲少女瑪莎·米爾斯命名。自二〇二四年實施以來，該制度已接獲數千通電話，並潛在地挽救了數百條生命。預計在二〇二八年三月前，該計畫將全面覆蓋所有急診單位。

paragraphs.en: The National Health Service (NHS) in England is expanding a vital safety initiative known as "Martha's Rule" to every emergency department in the country. This system gives patients, their loved ones, and hospital staff the right to ask for an urgent second opinion if they believe a patient's health is getting worse and their concerns are not being heard by the current medical team. The expansion marks a major step in the NHS's goal to make patient safety a top priority.
paragraphs.zh: 英國的國民保健署（NHS）正將一項名為「瑪莎條款」（Martha's Rule）的重要安全計畫，擴展至全國所有的急診部門。這項制度賦予病患、其親屬及醫院工作人員一項權利：若他們認為病患的健康狀況正在惡化，且目前的醫療團隊未採納他們的擔憂，便可要求進行緊急的第二醫療意見諮詢。此次擴展標誌著國民保健署將病患安全列為首要目標的重大進展。

paragraphs.en: "Martha's Rule" is named after 13-year-old Martha Mills, who died in 2021 at King's College Hospital in London. According to the BBC, Martha had been in the hospital following a bicycle accident that caused serious injuries. During her stay, she developed an infection and signs of sepsis—a dangerous condition where the body reacts too strongly to an infection, which can lead to organ failure. A coroner later ruled that Martha would likely have survived if she had been moved to intensive care sooner. Her parents, Merope Mills and Paul Laity, campaigned for years to change how hospitals listen to families, leading to the creation of this rule.
paragraphs.zh: 「瑪莎條款」是以十三歲的瑪莎·米爾斯（Martha Mills）命名，她於二〇二一年在倫敦的國王學院醫院（King's College Hospital）過世。根據英國廣播公司（BBC）報導，瑪莎當時因騎腳踏車發生意外導致重傷而住院。住院期間，她受到感染並出現敗血症跡象——這是一種身體對感染反應過度，可能導致器官衰竭的危險病症。驗屍官隨後裁定，若瑪莎能更早轉入加護病房，她極有可能存活。她的父母梅洛普·米爾斯（Merope Mills）與保羅·萊蒂（Paul Laity）多年來奔走呼籲，要求改變醫院傾聽家屬意見的方式，最終促成了這項條款的誕生。

paragraphs.en: Under this system, people in hospitals can call a dedicated phone number to trigger a "rapid review" of their care. This means a different medical team will examine the patient's situation and recommend any necessary changes. The Guardian reports that in the first 16 months since the rule was introduced in England in 2024, helplines received more than 10,000 calls. These calls have potentially saved 446 lives by leading to faster transfers to intensive care, the delivery of necessary medicines, or other life-saving treatments.
paragraphs.zh: 在此制度下，醫院內的人員可以撥打專線電話，啟動對病患照護情況的「快速審查」。這意味著另一組醫療團隊將會檢視病患的狀況，並建議任何必要的調整。《衛報》（The Guardian）報導指出，自二〇二四年該條款在英格蘭實施以來，在最初的十六個月內，專線已接獲超過一萬通電話。這些通話透過促成更迅速的加護病房轉診、提供必要藥物或其他救命治療，已潛在地挽救了四百四十六條生命。

paragraphs.en: Prof Aidan Fowler, the national director of patient safety at NHS England, described the expansion as a "critical new lifeline." He noted that emergency departments see some of the most vulnerable patients, making the ability to quickly raise concerns about a patient's condition essential. The BBC cited Prof Fowler saying that early testing shows the rule works well in busy emergency rooms, building on the success already seen in adult and children’s wards across the country.
paragraphs.zh: 英國國民保健署的國家病患安全主任艾丹·福勒教授（Prof Aidan Fowler）將此次擴展形容為「關鍵的新生命線」。他指出，急診部門接收的病患往往最為脆弱，因此能夠針對病患狀況迅速提出疑慮至關重要。英國廣播公司引述福勒教授的話表示，早期測試顯示該條款在繁忙的急診室中運作良好，並延續了該國成人與兒童病房已取得的成功經驗。

paragraphs.en: This expansion follows a successful eight-month pilot program at seven hospital trusts. During this trial, 69 calls were made to the dedicated lines, which resulted in some patients receiving immediate surgery or being moved to intensive care units. The government plans to complete the rollout across all emergency departments by March 2028. Health minister Baroness Merron stated that this initiative is part of a wider effort to keep patient safety at the heart of the NHS.
paragraphs.zh: 此次擴展是在七個醫院信託機構進行為期八個月的試點計畫成功後所推行的。在試驗期間，專線共接獲六十九通電話，促使部分病患獲得立即手術或轉入加護病房。政府計畫在二〇二八年三月前，完成全國所有急診部門的推廣工作。衛生部長梅隆女男爵（Baroness Merron）表示，這項計畫是將病患安全置於國民保健署核心地位的廣泛努力之一。

paragraphs.en: Beyond England, other parts of the United Kingdom are also looking at similar systems. The BBC reports that Scotland has already begun using Martha's Rule, while Northern Ireland is considering it. Wales already has a similar program in place called "Call4Concern." Matthew Hopkins, a director at the NHS Alliance, noted that health leaders across the system support the move, viewing it as a positive change for patient care.
paragraphs.zh: 除了英格蘭之外，英國的其他地區也正在研擬類似的制度。英國廣播公司報導，蘇格蘭已開始採用「瑪莎條款」，而北愛爾蘭也正在考慮跟進。威爾斯則已實施一項名為「呼籲關注」（Call4Concern）的類似計畫。國民保健署聯盟（NHS Alliance）的主管馬修·霍普金斯（Matthew Hopkins）指出，整個醫療系統的領導者皆支持此舉，並將其視為病患照護的一項正面變革。

paragraphs.en: For patients and their families, the process of using Martha's Rule is designed to be straightforward. The Guardian explains that those who are worried about their care or the care of a loved one can check with their local hospital or NHS trust to see if the rule is active in their specific unit. This can usually be done by checking the hospital's website or by simply asking a member of the medical staff.
paragraphs.zh: 對於病患及其家屬而言，「瑪莎條款」的使用流程設計得相當簡便。《衛報》說明，若民眾對自己或親人的照護狀況感到擔憂，可以向當地的醫院或國民保健署信託機構查詢，確認該條款是否已在特定單位啟用。這通常只需透過查看醫院網站，或直接詢問醫療人員即可確認。

paragraphs.en: As the NHS continues to grow this program, the focus remains on preventing the kind of tragedy that Martha’s family experienced. By giving families a formal way to speak up, the NHS aims to ensure that no one feels ignored when they are most in need of help. The success of the program so far suggests that listening to patients and their families is not just good communication, but a proven way to save lives in busy hospital environments.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著國民保健署持續推廣此計畫，重點依然在於防止瑪莎家人所經歷的那種悲劇再次發生。透過賦予家屬正式的發聲管道，國民保健署旨在確保沒有人在最需要幫助時感到被忽視。該計畫目前的成功顯示，傾聽病患及其家屬的聲音不僅是良好的溝通，更是繁忙醫院環境中被證實能挽救生命的有效途徑。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To cause an event or process to start or happen.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（扳機），這裡作動詞用。文中：Under this system, people in hospitals can call a dedicated phone number to trigger a "rapid review" of their care.

keyTerms.definitionEn: The official introduction of a new product, service, or system.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （新政策或產品的）正式推出、全面推行。
keyTerms.noteZh: 由動詞片語 roll out 轉變而來的名詞，指大規模的推行計畫。文中：The government plans to complete the rollout across all emergency departments by March 2028.

keyTerms.definitionEn: In the UK, administrative organizations that manage a group of hospitals.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （英國醫療體系中的）醫院信託機構、管理單位。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（信任）或名詞（信賴），這裡指英國醫療體系中的管理單位。文中：This expansion follows a successful eight-month pilot program at seven hospital trusts.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is the primary outcome of using the 'rapid review' system under Martha's Rule?

options.A: It allows families to sue the hospital for medical negligence.
options.B: It triggers an examination by a different medical team to recommend necessary changes.
options.C: It automatically transfers the patient to a different hospital facility.
options.D: It forces the original medical team to resign from the patient's care.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，該系統允許病患或家屬撥打專線，觸發「快速審查（rapid review）」，由另一個醫療團隊評估病患狀況並建議必要的調整。選項 A 文章未提及法律訴訟；選項 C 提到的是「轉入加護病房」而非「轉院」；選項 D 錯誤，因為該制度是為了改善照護品質，而非懲處原醫療團隊。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the medical care Martha Mills received before her death?

options.A: The medical team intentionally ignored her symptoms due to a lack of resources.
options.B: Her condition was too severe to be treated even with immediate intervention.
options.C: There was a disconnect between her family's concerns and the actions taken by the staff.
options.D: She died because the hospital lacked a dedicated phone line for emergencies.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第二段，驗屍官指出若 Martha 能更早轉入加護病房，她很可能存活，且其父母多年來致力於改變「醫院傾聽家屬聲音的方式」，這暗示了當時醫療團隊未能有效回應家屬對病情惡化的擔憂。選項 A 無證據顯示是「故意」忽視；選項 B 與驗屍官說法矛盾；選項 D 錯誤，因為當時尚未建立此制度，電話專線是該事件後的產物。

quiz.question: In the context of the article, what does the word 'trigger' mean in the sentence: '...to trigger a "rapid review" of their care'?

options.A: To cause an event or process to begin.
options.B: To aim a weapon at a specific target.
options.C: To provide a medical diagnosis for a patient.
options.D: To stop a procedure that is currently underway.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在此句中，trigger 作為動詞，意指「啟動」或「引發」某個程序。選項 B 是 trigger 作為名詞（扳機）的字面義，不符合上下文；選項 C 與診斷無關；選項 D 則剛好與原意相反，該制度是為了「開始」審查而非「停止」。

quiz.question: What is the central purpose of the NHS expanding 'Martha's Rule'?

options.A: To reduce the number of patients requiring intensive care units.
options.B: To replace the existing medical staff with more experienced specialists.
options.C: To standardize the way hospitals collect data on patient deaths.
options.D: To improve patient safety by ensuring families have a formal way to escalate concerns.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。全文的核心主旨都在討論 Martha's Rule 如何透過賦予病患與家屬「請求緊急第二意見」的權利，來確保他們的擔憂被聽見，進而提升醫療安全並挽救生命。選項 A 是結果之一而非目的；選項 B 與文章內容無關；選項 C 雖提到數據，但並非此政策的核心目標。
